title: Writing Clear Clinical Notes — SOAP, Consent and Safe Records

hook.en: Good notes protect patients, colleagues and you. Learn a simple SOAP structure, what must always be recorded and the habits that make a note useful a month later.
hook.ur: Achhe notes mareezon, saathiyon aur aap ki hifazat karte hain. Saada SOAP dhancha, jo hamesha likhna hai aur woh aadatein seekhein jo note ko ek mahine baad bhi mufeed banati hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll write a SOAP note with measurable findings and a clear plan, record consent, safety screening and advice, and keep patient information private.
goal.ur: End tak aap naapne ke qabil findings aur saaf plan ke saath SOAP note likhenge, razamandi, hifazati screening aur mashwara likhenge, aur mareez ki maloomat ko mehfooz rakhenge.

text.en: A clinical note is a **record of what happened and why**, written so that another clinician could continue the care. A **SOAP** note has four parts: **Subjective** (what the patient tells you), **Objective** (what you measure and observe), **Assessment** (what you think and why) and **Plan** (what you will do and when). Notes should be **clear, dated, signed and written soon after the visit**.
text.ur: Clinical note **jo hua aur kyun hua uska record** hai, aise likha jaye ke doosra clinician care jaari rakh sake. **SOAP** note ke chaar hissay hain: **Subjective** (mareez ne kya bataya), **Objective** (aap ne kya naapa aur dekha), **Assessment** (aap kya sochte hain aur kyun) aur **Plan** (kya karenge aur kab). Notes **saaf, tareekh wale, dastkhat shuda aur visit ke jaldi baad likhe** hone chahiye.

text.en: Think of a note as **a letter to the next clinician**, who may be you in three weeks with forty other patients in between. If you wrote "knee pain, treated, better", the letter says nothing. If you wrote "pain 6 to 3 out of 10, bend 90 to 105 degrees after heel slides, plan strengthening", the letter lets care continue.
text.ur: Note ko **agle clinician ko likha khat** samjhein, jo teen haftay baad chalis mareezon ke baad khud aap ho sakte hain. "Knee dard, ilaj, behtar" likha to khat kuch nahi batata. "Dard 6 se 3, heel slides ke baad bend 90 se 105 degree, plan strengthening" likha to care jaari rakhi ja sakti hai.

steps.title: Subjective
steps.detail: Record the main complaint in the patient's words, how it began, what changes it, the 24-hour pattern, medical history, medicines and goals. Note the safety screening you did. || Subjective

steps.title: Objective
steps.detail: Write measurements, not impressions: range in degrees, strength grades, girth in centimetres, test results (positive or negative), outcome measure scores and what you observed. || Objective

steps.title: Assessment
steps.detail: State your clinical impression, the evidence for it, the main alternatives you considered and the patient's response to treatment. Link it to the goals. || Assessment

steps.title: Plan
steps.detail: Write the treatment given, advice and home exercises, referrals, outcome measures to repeat and when you will review. Record consent and that you explained the plan. || Plan

question.en: Which entry belongs in the Objective part of a SOAP note?
question.ur: SOAP note ke Objective hissay mein kaun si entry aati hai?

feedback.en: That is what the patient says, so it is subjective.
feedback.ur: Yeh mareez ka bayan hai, is liye subjective hai.

text.en: Knee flexion 105 degrees, extension lag 5 degrees, quadriceps grade 4
text.ur: Knee flexion 105 degree, extension lag 5 degree, quadriceps grade 4

feedback.en: Yes — measurements and observations are objective.
feedback.ur: Haan — paimaish aur mushahida objective hain.

title.en: A weak note or a useful note?

rows.en: "No fever, calf soft, wound dry; red-flag questions negative"
rows.ur: "Bukhar nahi, pindli naram, zakhm khushk; red-flag sawal negative"

rows.en: "Heel slides and cycling daily; review Friday; refer if flexion below 90"
rows.ur: "Heel slides aur cycling rozana; juma review; flexion 90 se kam ho to refer"

text.en: **Measure, date, sign, explain.** Numbers beat adjectives, every entry is dated and signed, and the note says what the patient was told and agreed.
text.ur: **Naapein, tareekh, dastkhat, samjhayein.** Numbers sifaat se behtar hain, har entry par tareekh aur dastkhat hote hain, aur note batata hai mareez ko kya bataya gaya aur woh kis par razi hua.

text.en: **Writing opinions as facts or leaving gaps.** "Patient is lazy" or "non-compliant" is an opinion that harms trust and can be used against you. Describe what happened ("did not complete the exercises because of work hours") and never alter or remove an old entry; add a dated correction.
text.ur: **Raaye ko haqeeqat likhna ya khali jagah chhorna.** "Mareez susst hai" ya "hidayat nahi manta" raaye hai jo bharosa kharab karti hai aur aap ke khilaf istemal ho sakti hai. Jo hua likhein ("kaam ke ghanton ki wajah se exercises mukammal nahi kiye") aur purani entry kabhi na badlein ya hatayein; tareekh ke saath tasheeh shamil karein.

question.en: A patient says the pain is gone and you did not examine them that day. What should the note say?
question.ur: Mareez kehta hai dard khatam hai aur us din aap ne examine nahi kiya. Note mein kya likhna chahiye?

text.en: Record what the patient reported and that no examination was done
text.ur: Mareez ne jo bataya aur yeh ke examination nahi hua likhein

feedback.en: Yes — a note must be honest about what was and was not done.
feedback.ur: Haan — note ko imandari se batana chahiye ke kya hua aur kya nahi.

text.ur: Phir bhi normal findings likh dein

question.en: How should patient records be kept?
question.ur: Mareez ke records kaise rakhne chahiye?

text.en: Photos of notes shared on a group chat for help
text.ur: Madad ke liye notes ki tasveerein group chat mein bhejna

feedback.ur: Yeh raaz daari tor deta hai.

text.en: Private, secure, shared only with those involved in the care or with consent
text.ur: Pur-raaz, mehfooz, sirf care mein shamil logon ya razamandi ke saath share

feedback.en: Yes — confidentiality is a basic duty.
feedback.ur: Haan — raaz daari buniyadi farz hai.

text.en: Left open on a shared computer

**Write while it is fresh.** Make brief notes during the visit and finish within the day. Use a template with headings so you do not forget safety questions, consent and the review date. If a patient asks to see their record, follow your clinic's policy and be ready to explain it.
text.ur: **Taaza hote hi likhein.** Visit ke dauran mukhtasar notes lein aur usi din mukammal karein. Headings wala template istemal karein taake hifazati sawal, razamandi aur review ki tareekh na bhoolein. Mareez apna record dekhna chahe to clinic ki policy par chalein aur samjhane ke liye tayyar rahein.

question.en: Why are measurable findings more useful than descriptions?
question.ur: Naapne ke qabil findings bayanon se zyada mufeed kyun hain?

answer.en: Numbers let you and others see change over time, judge whether it is real and justify treatment decisions. Words like "better" or "stiff" mean different things to different people and cannot be compared at the next visit.
answer.ur: Numbers aap ko aur doosron ko waqt ke saath tabdeeli dekhne, uske asli hone ka andaza lagane aur ilaj ke faislon ka jawaaz dene dete hain. "Behtar" ya "akhra" jaise alfaz mukhtalif logon ke liye mukhtalif maani rakhte hain aur agli visit par muqabla nahi ho sakte.

beats.patient: After a knee replacement visit, a student writes "knee better, walks well, continue". A senior colleague takes over next week and cannot tell whether the patient is safe to progress.
beats.assessment: The note lacks measurements, safety screening and a plan, so the care cannot continue safely.
beats.treatment: Rewrite with ranges, strength, calf and wound checks, walking aid, goals, advice given and a review date.
beats.reassess: The colleague reads the note, sees the knee is progressing and plans the next stage with confidence.

text.en: **Never falsify, alter or destroy a record.** Make a dated correction instead. Record any safety concern, referral or adverse event clearly and report it as your clinic requires. Protect passwords, lock screens and paper files, and do not share identifiable details in public chats or social media.
text.ur: **Record kabhi jaali na banayein, na badlein, na mitayein.** Is ke bajaye tareekh ke saath tasheeh likhein. Koi hifazati fikr, referral ya manfi waqiya saaf likhein aur clinic ki zaroorat ke mutabiq report karein. Passwords, screen lock aur kaghazi files ki hifazat karein, aur pehchan wali tafseel public chats ya social media par share na karein.

summary.en: A SOAP note records what the patient says (subjective), what you measure (objective), your reasoning (assessment) and your plan.
summary.ur: SOAP note mareez ka bayan (subjective), aap ki paimaish (objective), aap ki reasoning (assessment) aur plan likhta hai.

summary.en: Use measurable findings, record consent, safety screening, advice and the review date, and sign and date every entry.
summary.ur: Naapne ke qabil findings istemal karein, razamandi, hifazati screening, mashwara aur review ki tareekh likhein, aur har entry par dastkhat aur tareekh dalein.

summary.en: Never alter old entries or write opinions as facts, and keep patient information private.
summary.ur: Purani entries kabhi na badlein aur raaye ko haqeeqat na likhein, aur mareez ki maloomat pur-raaz rakhein.

front.en: How do you correct an old entry?

back.en: Add a dated correction; never delete or change the original.
back.ur: Tareekh ke saath tasheeh shamil karein; asal ko kabhi na mitayein.

back.en: It shows the patient understood and agreed to the plan.
back.ur: Yeh dikhata hai ke mareez ne plan samjha aur manzoor kiya.

note.en: Choose measures you can record and compare.
note.ur: Aise measures chunein jo likh kar muqabla kiye ja sakein.

note.en: Write the reasoning behind your assessment.
note.ur: Apne assessment ke peechay ki reasoning likhein.
